newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May industrial output rose 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May industrial output rose 0.4 pct.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board report of U.S. industrial production and capacity utilization, seasonally adjusted.
Total Industrial: May Apr Mar Feb May97/96

Wall Street economists had expected May industrial production to rise 0.2 percent and estimated that May capacity use would be at a rate of 83.4 percent.
The 83.7 percent capacity use rate registered in May was the highest in more than 1-1/2 years, since 83.9 percent in September 1995.

The Fed said production of motor vehicles partly rebounded in May, when a strike against General Motors Corp ended. It also said that continued strength in output of commercial aircraft and in production of high-technology products contributed to widespread gains for durable goods producers.
Motor vehicle assemblies rose in May to a rate of 5.8 million a year for cars from 5.7 million in April. For light trucks the assembly rate was up to 5.4 million in May from 5.3 million in April.

Utilities output was down sharply by 1.9 percent in May after a 2.3 percent jump in April. The Fed said that relatively cool temperatures last month reduced the need for air conditioning and kept electricity demand down.
